builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Beyond Leaderboard Ranks: Selecting Software Engineering Agents Under Budget Constraints
summary: It replaces exhaustive full-benchmark evaluation and leaderboard-rank-based agent selection with an uncertainty-aware adaptive allocation strategy (successive halving) that accounts for statistical indistinguishability and validated execution costs. It costs additional evaluation infrastructure and complexity, and its advantage narrows when task costs are unknown before execution or when exact-best selection is required. Reported agent costs can differ from standardized token-based estimates by up to 11.7x, and selective task evaluation can bias full-benchmark cost estimates, so cost validation can fail if these factors are ignored.
rationale: It directly enables a small team with a limited budget to select a software engineering agent for production at a fraction of the evaluation cost while explicitly managing statistical uncertainty.
technique: Budget-constrained agent selection via successive halving

claims.statement: It replaces exhaustive full-benchmark evaluation and leaderboard-rank-based agent selection with an uncertainty-aware adaptive allocation strategy (successive halving) that accounts for statistical indistinguishability and validated execution costs. It costs additional evaluation infrastructure and complexity, and its advantage narrows when task costs are unknown before execution or when exact-best selection is required. Reported agent costs can differ from standardized token-based estimates by up to 11.7x, and selective task evaluation can bias full-benchmark cost estimates, so cost validation can fail if these factors are ignored.

Successive halving reaches the uncertainty-aware selection target on SWE-bench using 6.6% of exhaustive evaluation spend (a ~15.2x reduction), with the lowest cost on six of seven benchmarks and a tie on the seventh.
